sovereign_country.strategic_role: 全球跨境基金设立第一大国、超大型跨国投资架构

business_scope.primary_industry_name: Commercial Mail Receiving Agency (CMRA) and Digital Scanning

applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Belgium-Luxembourg Economic Union (BLEU) bilateral investment treaty network
Luxembourg-United States Income Tax Treaty (1996, as amended by 2009 and 2018 protocols)
Luxembourg-United Kingdom Double Taxation Agreement (1967, as amended)
Germany-Luxembourg Double Taxation Agreement (1990, as amended)
European Union legal order (TFEU freedoms and EU investment agreements applicable in Luxembourg)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Loi modifiée du 12 novembre 2004 relative à la lutte contre le blanchiment et contre le financement du terrorisme; Loi du 13 janvier 2019 instituant un Registre des bénéficiaires effectifs; Règlement grand-ducal implementing the UBO register law; Code de commerce as amended by the Law of 10 August 1915 on commercial companies; CSSF Regulation 12-02 and subsequent AML/CFT circulars.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified copy of passport (national identity document) of each beneficial owner, partner and authorized representative
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent national passport authority of the individual's country of nationality
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (1961 Convention) if the issuing jurisdiction is a party to the convention; otherwise consular legalization by the Luxembourg embassy or consulate.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of good conduct (extrait du casier judiciaire) of each manager (gérant) and officer
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Luxembourg criminal records office or equivalent judicial authority in the individual's state of residence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or consular legalization, followed by notarized translation into French, German or English.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of legal existence and good standing for each corporate partner/shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent trade or company registry of the corporate partner's jurisdiction of incorporation
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or consular legalization; notarially certified translation if not in French/German/English.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Board resolution or equivalent corporate resolution authorizing the Luxembourg SCSp formation and appointment of the general partner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Board of directors or general meeting of the ultimate corporate partner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or consular legalization, depending on the country of execution; where the resolution is signed before a notary, notarization suffices for EU signatories.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference letter or certificate for the initial capital contributor (where a bank account is opened)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Licensed bank or credit institution holding the contributor's account
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Signed by an authorized bank officer and notarized if required by the Luxembourg AML file; apostille/consular legalization not necessary for EEA banks.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: All partners, managers, beneficial owners and authorized signatories are screened prior to incorporation against: (i) the consolidated European Union restrictive measures lists and UN Security Council sanctions; (ii) the Luxembourg national sanctions list issued under the Ministry of Finance; (iii) the US OFAC Specially Designated Nationals and Blocked Persons List when any US dollar clearing, US payment rail or US counterparty is reasonably expected; (iv) the UK Consolidated List where Sterling or UK payment services are used; and (v) political-exposed-persons (PEP) databases in line with FATF Recommendation 12. Enhanced due diligence and source-of-wealth investigations are mandatory for any PEP, high-risk third-country connection, or negative sanction/OFAC hit. Screening results are documented and retained for at least five years after termination of the business relationship.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) / Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS) e-filing portal at https://www.lbr.lu
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The proposed name must be entered exclusively in Latin characters. Non-Latin script names are transliterated phonetically into the Latin alphabet and the governing statute text (contrat de société) is drawn in French or in a Luxembourg-recognized administrative language. The legal suffix 'SCSp' or the full form 'Société en commandite spéciale' must appear in the company name. Names are assessed for distinctiveness, misleading character, and compliance with the Law of 10 August 1915 on commercial companies, as amended.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: BANK, BANCA, BANQUE, CRÉDIT, CREDIT (require CSSF / Ministry of Finance authorization)
ASSURANCE, INSURANCE, RÉASSURANCE, REINSURANCE (require insurance supervisory authorization)
SICAV, SICAF, SIF, RAIF, UCITS, INVESTMENT FUND (subject to CSSF licensing or registration unless clearly used for an unregulated single-investor family vehicle)
ETAT, STATE, NATIONAL, LUXEMBOURG, MUNICIPAL, COMMUNE (require ministerial or Grand-Ducal approval)
UNIVERSITY, UNIVERSITÉ, ÉCOLE, CHAMBRE, INSPECTION, RED CROSS (protected by legislative or international conventions)
SA, SARL, SCA, SCS, SCSp (legal-form indicators may only be used when the corresponding legal form is adopted)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: In the event of a rejection, the applicant may within fifteen days of the RCS decision file a reasoned request for reconsideration with the Luxembourg Business Registers, attaching the proposed statutes and a submission distinguishing the proposed name from conflicting names. If the initial rejection is maintained, the applicant may appeal to the Luxembourg Administrative Tribunal within one month of notification of the final refusal, under the amended law on the jurisdiction of administrative courts. A formal written appeal is required, and an administrative-review counsel may be engaged for complex trademarks and protected tokens.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A registered office in Luxembourg is mandatory. A service provider's address may be used as the registered office, but a pure virtual-office arrangement without any operational staff or physical management will not satisfy the Luxembourg economic-substance expectations for an SCSp carrying on an active commercial mail-receiving and scanning activity. Such an arrangement is permissible only as a formal mailing address; actual daily business activity, administrative oversight, employees and relevant management decisions must be materialized in Luxembourg to sustain tax residence and avoid abuse-of-law challenges.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: 30-45% probability of an unannounced on-site physical inspection or a written substance questionnaire by the Luxembourg direct tax administration (ACD) or social security authorities within the first two years of operation; the likelihood increases to approximately 50-55% where the SCSp applies for a Luxembourg VAT number or makes continuous intra-EU supplies.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: RCS incorporation filing (lodging of the SCSp deed and required statutory annexes)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Official statutory filing fee for registrations under the Law of 10 August 1915

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Notarization and apostille/consular-legalization bundle for UBO and corporate documents

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Luxembourg notarial tariff and prevailing apostille/consular processing charges

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: UBO identification, PEP list, and global sanctions screening compliance package
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Eligible AML/CFT compliance provider or law firm
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing Luxembourg market benchmark (fixed fee or capped hourly fee)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Registered office / commercial correspondence address and mail scanning infrastructure (annual)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Independent Luxembourg registered-office and virtual-office service provider
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark for corporate mail scanning and registered office services in Luxembourg

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Tax registrations and social security employer registration handling
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Administration des contributions directes, Administration de l'enregistrement/TVA, and joint social security centre (CCSS)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Nil statutory fee; professional handling charged at prevailing market benchmark

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Amended Luxembourg Law of 10 August 1915 on Commercial Companies (Loi du 10 août 1915 concernant les sociétés commerciales), Title II, Chapter III, Articles 14-1 to 14-11 (Société en Commandite Spéciale), as introduced by the Law of 23 July 2016; Grand-Ducal Regulation of 12 August 2016 on the RCS procedure
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers – Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: SCSp partnership agreement (contrat de société) and subscription sheets filed via the RCS online e-filing portal
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum capital for an SCSp; the partnership capital is freely determined in the partnership agreement. Because the SCSp has no legal personality, contributions are contractually defined and no escrow account is required by Luxembourg law.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED that the undersigned general partner hereby constitutes a Société en Commandite Spéciale under the amended Luxembourg Law of 10 August 1915 upon execution of the SCSp partnership agreement. The general partner accepts all subscriptions listed in the subscription schedule; no statutory minimum capital applies. The registered office is hereby adopted at the address identified in the partnership agreement and may be relocated by simple manager decision. [Name] is appointed manager (associé gérant) with full authority to operate the virtual office and mail-scanning business, to open and manage payment processing accounts, and to represent the SCSp. The manager is expressly authorized to file the incorporation dossier with the RCS, pay official fees, and apply for the autorisation d'établissement and all ancillary registrations.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution of the SCSp Partnership Agreement and Subscriptions
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Parties' private instrument; no mandatory notarization under Article 14-3 of the amended Law of 10 August 1915
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the partnership agreement in English or French, defining the entity name, registered office, corporate object (ISIC 8299 / NAICS 561431 virtual office and mail scanning), duration, capital, profit-sharing, powers of the general partner, and identity of limited partners. Ensure execution by the general partner and at least one limited partner; the SCSp may be formed by private writing; verify signatures and date of execution.
required_dossiers: Proof of address of registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a partner refuses to sign or a defect is identified, renegotiate and re-execute an amended agreement; this is a contractual step with no registry action required until filing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Electronic Filing of the Incorporation Dossier with the Luxembourg Trade and Companies Register
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers – Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS) online e-filing portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Within one month of execution of the partnership agreement, submit the incorporation filing through the Luxembourg Business Registers online platform, attaching the signed partnership agreement, subscription sheets, occupancy proof for the registered office, the general partner's criminal record extract and declaration of non-bankruptcy, and a power of attorney if represented. Verify the proposed entity name for availability via the LBR search tool and pay the EUR 24 filing fee.
required_dossiers: Registered office occupancy certificate or lease
Criminal record extract (casier judiciaire) of the general partner
Declaration of non-bankruptcy of the general partner
Notarized power of attorney, if applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the RCS issues a deficiency notice (défaut), cure the file within the stated grace period, typically 8 days, by resubmitting corrected documents; a rejection may be remedied by amending and resubmitting the filing or by appeal to the Luxembourg District Court.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Publication in the Electronic Compendium (RESA) and Issuance of RCS Excerpt
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS) / Recueil électronique des sociétés et associations (RESA)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon successful registration, the RCS publishes the statutory excerpt in the RESA and issues the RCS registration number and national registration number. Download the certified RCS excerpt (extrait du RCS) and the published abstract; these documents are required for the establishment permit, VAT registration, and bank account opening.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the RESA publication is delayed, contact the RCS helpdesk with the filing receipt; if the published excerpt contains inaccuracies, submit a rectification filing with the RCS.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Beneficial Owner Declaration in the Luxembourg RBE Register
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registre des bénéficiaires effectifs (RBE) – Luxembourg Business Registers
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Within one month of RCS registration, file the beneficial ownership declaration online on the RBE platform, identifying every individual who ultimately owns or controls the SCSp. Provide the ownership schedule and supporting identification documents; the declaration is accessible to tax authorities, AML supervisors, and financial institutions performing due diligence.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the RBE flags the declaration, provide clarifications within 15 days of the notice; where control attribution is disputed, submit a written justification to the RCS for review.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Application for Business Establishment Permit (Autorisation d'établissement)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Ministry of the Economy – Direction générale des Classes moyennes (Middle Classes Department), Luxembourg
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the application for the autorisation d'établissement via the MyGuichet.lu portal, designating the regulated commercial activity of commercial mail receiving agency and scanning services. The general partner must demonstrate good repute and lawful residence or appointment of a Luxembourg legal representative; provide the RCS excerpt, premises lease, financial capacity evidence, and criminal record certificate. The Ministry of the Economy issues the permit, which is mandatory for the commercial operation of the virtual office and mail scanning activity.
required_dossiers: Luxembourg legal representative appointment, if applicable
Certificate of good conduct (bonne conduite, vie privée)
Business plan and financial capacity evidence
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Ministry issues a supplementary information request, respond within one month to avoid automatic rejection; an express refusal may be appealed to the Luxembourg Administrative Tribunal within three months of notification.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: VAT, Social Security, and Ancillary Registrations
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT); Centre commun de la sécurité sociale (CCSS)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the SCSp for Luxembourg VAT (RC TVA) using the MyGuichet.lu e-service; register as an employer with the CCSS if staff will be hired; request an EORI number if any mail parcels will cross EU borders. Open a dedicated Luxembourg bank account and complete the AML KYC file, disclosing the target recurring payment rails (Stripe recurring and credit card) as the principal collection channels.
required_dossiers: Bank account details and KYC documentation
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the AEDT delays or rejects the VAT file, submit proof of the initial filing and escalate to the AEDT registration office for written confirmation; incorrect EORI data may be corrected with the Customs and Excise Agency (ADA).

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministry of the Economy – Direction générale des Classes moyennes (Middle Classes Department), Luxembourg
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Autorisation d'établissement (Business Establishment Permit) under the amended Law of 2 September 2011 regulating access to the professions of artisan, merchant, manufacturer, and certain liberal professions

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt from full EIA – office/CMRA activity classified as low-impact and subject only to general registration and waste-management obligations
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No process wastewater or VOC emissions expected; compliance required with Grand-Ducal Regulation on office waste separation, packaging waste, and WEEE (electronic equipment) disposal; municipal waste collection fees apply; no IED/IPPC permit required.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety inspection and certification of the premises by the Administration des services de secours (Fire and Rescue Service); occupational health and safety registration with the Inspection du Travail et des Mines (ITM); structural load certification of the registered office area where mezzanine or heavy scanning equipment is installed.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Administration des Contributions Directes (ACD) for direct taxes and Administration de l'Enregistrement, des Domaines et de la TVA (AEDT) for value added tax; business registrations, filings, and payments are effected through the MyGuichet.lu secure portal and the Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) platform issuing the RCS matricule.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: The SCSp is registered with the Luxembourg Trade and Companies Register (Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés - RCS) through MyGuichet.lu to obtain a 13-digit national business registration number (matricule). Upon obtaining the matricule, the SCSp must file the statutory VAT registration application with the AEDT to receive a Luxembourg TVA identification number. Non-resident foreign entities supplying taxable services into Luxembourg may apply for a Luxembourg TVA number directly via the AEDT cross-border procedure or through a Luxembourg-approved tax representative, submitting the certified RCS extract, constitutive documents, passports of managing partners, and evidence of the Luxembourg economic nexus or service-provision supply chain.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Luxembourg does not operate a US-style check-the-box regime. The SCSp is statutorily fiscally transparent for corporate income tax and net wealth tax purposes; partners are taxed directly on their profit share per the partnership agreement. Available elections and structural mechanisms include: (i) VAT group (fiscal unity) election for eligible Luxembourg taxable persons; (ii) voluntary VAT registration to waive the EUR 35,000 small-business franchise exemption; (iii) contractual profit-allocation provisions in the limited partnership agreement determining tax attribution; and (iv) ATAD and EU anti-hybrid assessments requiring partners to reconcile the Luxembourg transparent classification with their residence-jurisdiction classifications to avoid hybrid mismatches.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT (Taxe sur la Valeur Ajoutée - TVA), fully harmonized with the EU VAT Directive
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: VAT registration is compulsory upon start of any taxable economic activity in Luxembourg; however, the small-business franchise (franchise de base) exempts businesses with an annual turnover not exceeding EUR 35,000 (exclusive of VAT) from VAT charging obligations, while still allowing voluntary registration to recover input VAT.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Luxembourg imposes no real-time fiscal clearance or digital stamping mandate for domestic B2B invoicing. Electronic invoicing is mandatory only for B2G transactions, which must be transmitted in the EN 16931 standardized format via the national PEPPOL access point. The EU 'VAT in the Digital Age' (ViDA) proposal is expected to introduce mandatory cross-border and domestic B2B electronic invoicing and digital transaction reporting in phases from 2028 onward; the SCSp should architect its billing platform to be PEPPOL/EN16931-compliant in advance.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exports of physical goods to destinations outside the EU qualify for the 0% VAT export exemption provided the goods are dispatched or transported out of Luxembourg within the statutory period and supported by corroborating evidence of physical exit. Electronically supplied services, including digitized mail scanning and virtual office deliverables supplied to a foreign business customer, are not goods exports; they follow the B2B place-of-supply rule requiring the Luxembourg supplier to obtain and retain commercial evidence of the customer's business establishment, with the customer's jurisdiction applying tax reverse-charge mechanisms where relevant. Back-office document processing and mail management services physically performed in Luxembourg for non-EU principals qualify for the 0% regime under Luxembourg place-of-supply provisions for services rendered to customers established outside the EU, provided the evidentiary documentation is maintained. No national FX repatriation statutory deadline exists under Luxembourg law; the 180-day inward remittance window is the documentary-credit benchmark applied in administrative and audit practice.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (SAD / EU Single Administrative Document) endorsed by the Luxembourg Customs Administration (Administration des Douanes et Accises)
Bill of Lading or alternative transport instrument (CMR waybill / Air Waybill) evidencing the physical dispatch from Luxembourg
Inward Remittance Certificate / bank transfer evidence demonstrating the receipt of consideration by the Luxembourg SCSp
Commercial invoice and packing list incorporating the direct-export statement
Foreign customer's written confirmation of business establishment and non-EU status, including the customer's VAT identification or equivalent registration number
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Luxembourg customs and tax authorities conduct ex-post documentary audits of export zero-rating claims. If the required proof of physical removal or payment is defective or absent, the AEDT retroactively applies the standard VAT rate (17% or the applicable reduced rate) to the supply, together with late-interest computed from the date of supply, and may levy administrative penalties of up to EUR 4,000 per infringement. In cases of fraudulent or sham export arrangements, criminal fines and imprisonment may apply under Luxembourg VAT legislation, and the full VAT amount may be clawed back from the SCSp jointly and severally with its partners. All export zero-rating evidence files must be retained for at least ten years.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque centrale du Luxembourg (BCL) / Luxembourg Ministry of Finance, operating within the Eurosystem and in coordination with the CSSF (Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier) for payment services and financial crime supervision
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Luxembourg maintains full convertibility for both current and capital account transactions under EU free movement of capital (TFEU Article 63). There is no exchange control approval requirement for inbound capital contributions, profit distribution, dividend remittance, or repayment of shareholder loans. Profit remittance is unrestricted in euros, and foreign-currency accounts may be held freely; practical hurdles arise only from AML/KYC documentation standards, tax compliance declarations for withholding, and EU or UN sanctions screening. The euro is fully legal tender, and the SCSp may maintain accounts in EUR or any eligible foreign currency at licensed credit institutions.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: There are no mandatory export proceeds surrender rules or minimum conversion ratios in Luxembourg. Luxembourg does not impose foreign-exchange surrender obligations on export receipts; all export proceeds may be retained in foreign currency or converted freely through an authorised credit institution. The only duty is standard balance-of-payments reporting to the BCL for direct investment and cross-border transaction statistics where applicable.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: Medium for EEA-licensed e-money institutions (EMIs) that hold a valid passport into Luxembourg under the revised EU Payment Services Directive (PSD2); Low for offshore or non-EEA digital EMIs. An offshore EMI may not lawfully provide payment accounts or execute payments for a Luxembourg SCSp unless it holds an authorised Luxembourg branch or passporting European licence. The virtual-office/CMRA activity profile is classified as higher-risk under EBA AML guidelines, and most offshore EMIs will decline the relationship or restrict transaction limits where physical substance is limited. Practical viability requires the EMI to be regulated by an EU/EEA authority, to accept a Luxembourg-registered SCSp as customer without legal personality, and to provide compliant IBAN, SEPA access, and SWIFT handling.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical presence is the prevailing market standard for SCSp vehicles. The general partner (or its duly authorised manager), signatories, and ultimate beneficial owners must attend an in-person KYC interview at the Luxembourg bank or a recognised embassy/consulate, especially where the client uses a virtual office and mail-scanning service. Remote video identification is permitted under certain CSSF-accepted processes, but in practice it is reserved for low-risk, fully transparent structures; banks retain discretion to require a physical meeting without delay. A bank-issued questionnaire, notarised partnership agreement, beneficial ownership declaration, and proof of economic purpose are mandatory.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Registered office mismatch and non-face-to-face virtual office establishment
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Lease/registered-office agreement for the Luxembourg address; utility bill in the entity name; certified CMRA license under Luxembourg commercial regulations; RBE (Registre des bénéficiaires effectifs) extract; notarised SCSp partnership agreement; board/general partner resolution approving the account; detailed operating description of the mail-scanning and digital forwarding workflow; organisational chart with the general partner and service provider.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unclear source of funds for capital contributions and anticipated transaction flows
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Bank statements of contributing partners; source-of-wealth questionnaire; source-of-funds letters; capital call documentation; audited or management financial statements of investors; economic substance map showing real business activity; projected transaction volume and counterparty list; explanation of target payment rails (Stripe recurring and credit card transactions) and expected settlement currency flows.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Pass-through partnership with opaque beneficial ownership chain
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Beneficial ownership register extract from Luxembourg RBE; full ownership cascade with percentages; identification documents and residential proof for all natural-person ultimate beneficial owners; organisational charts of any corporate general partner; legal opinion on SCSp formation and authority; declaration of no shell-company misuse; sanction/PEP screening results of all owners and operators.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-risk jurisdictional exposure or sanctions-linked counterparties in subscription/merchant flows
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Independent risk rating with supporting evidence; complete counterparty list with nationality and jurisdiction analysis; FATCA/CRS classifications and self-certifications; transaction flow diagrams for inbound capital and outbound merchant discretions; legal opinions where relevant on economic purpose and sanctions compliance; independent audit trail for recurring card payments processed through a reputable payment service provider.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound capital injections into the SCSp are routed through regulated banks or authorised payment institutions via standard SWIFT MT103 for foreign-currency transfers or SEPA Credit Transfer for euro-denominated contributions from EEA accounts. No exchange-control permit is required. Each transfer must include a clear purpose reference such as 'SCSp capital contribution - LU__LU__LU_SCSP__ISIC_8299_02_VIRTUAL_OFFICE_MAIL_SCANNING', the Luxembourg tax identification number of the entity, and the remitter/beneficiary legal names. The receiving Luxembourg bank verifies the identity of the remitter and beneficiary, confirms beneficial ownership details against the RBE, and applies enhanced due diligence where the contribution originates from a third-country jurisdiction. Any cross-border direct investment flow is subject to applicable BCL balance-of-payments statistical reporting and CSSF AML record-keeping requirements.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound trade and operating disbursements are executed via SEPA Credit Transfer within the EU/EEA, SWIFT MT103 for non-EUR payments, and commercial documentary letters of credit (MT700 series) where goods or services are sourced from third countries. For the virtual-office/mail-scanning business, routine monthly expenses such as rent, scanning software subscriptions, and payment processor fees are settled by SEPA direct debit or SWIFT MT103 depending on destination; commercial LC usage is limited to higher-value physical imports and requires a fully cash-backed or credit-approved facility at the Luxembourg relationship bank. All outbound payments must be supported by invoices, service agreements, and proper tax documentation, with purpose references matching the underlying commercial transaction.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Outright deliverable FX forwards on major convertible currencies (EUR/USD, EUR/GBP, EUR/CHF)
FX swaps between EUR and convertible currencies used for liquidity timing alignment
Cross-currency swaps to hedge long-term foreign-currency exposure on capital accounts or merchant settlement flows
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) solely where the underlying currency of a trade settlement or investment leg is non-convertible or subject to local remittance restrictions
Currency options (puts and calls) on permissible convertible currencies for contingency hedging of the SCSp's future trade receivables

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Beneficial Owner Confirmation (RBE déclaration confirmative)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers – Registre des Bénéficiaires Effectifs (RBE)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually by the registration anniversary date; any change in ownership or control must be filed within 30 days.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative fine up to EUR 125,000 for failure to file or for inaccurate declaration; publication of non-compliance may be ordered.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual accounts filing (dépôt des comptes annuels)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS) via the Luxembourg Business Registers platform
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within seven (7) months after the close of the financial year; e.g., for a 31 December year-end, by 31 July of the following year.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty ranging from EUR 100 to EUR 10,000; repeated default may lead to court-ordered compulsory dissolution and additional fines.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual partnership tax / informational return (déclaration d'impôt sur les sociétés ou déclaration d'information)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Administration des Contributions Directes (ACD) – Luxembourg tax administration
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: By 31 December of the year following the tax year; deadline extensions are available on request. A nil return is mandatory even where the partnership is fiscally transparent.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Default assessment by the tax office; administrative penalty up to 10% of the assessment (or EUR 150 per month per document for non-filing); partner-level taxes remain enforceable.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Business establishment permit renewal (autorisation d'établissement) for virtual office and mail-scanning activities
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Ministry of Economy – Directorate General for Industry and Commerce, Intellectual Property and Financial Inclusion
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annual renewal before the permit anniversary date; any change in authorised activity, managers, or premises requires immediate filing.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Carrying on the activity without a valid permit is subject to an administrative stop order and fines up to EUR 1,000 per day; criminal sanctions apply for persistent breaches.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: SCSp is generally exempt from statutory audit unless it exceeds two of the three following thresholds at balance sheet date: balance sheet total > EUR 6,250,000; net turnover > EUR 12,500,000; average number of employees > 50. An audit may also be requested by partners holding at least 10% of partnership interests or required by the articles / management agreement.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Luxembourg GAAP as set out in the Law of 19 July 2020 on commercial accounts (transposing the EU Accounting Directive 2013/34/EU). IFRS as adopted by the EU is permissible where required for a true and fair view or where the partnership is part of a listed group.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Annually, the SCSp must confirm the accuracy of its beneficial ownership details on the Luxembourg RBE platform by the anniversary of its registration. Every transfer of partnership interests triggering a change in ultimate ownership must be filed with the RBE within 30 days of the transfer, together with an updated partnership register. If no transfer occurs during the year, an annual confirmation is nonetheless mandatory.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Pledges and Encumbrances over Partnership Interests

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 1,200 – USD 2,500 per annum for registered office, domiciliation agent, and corporate secretarial services in Luxembourg
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 2,000 – USD 5,500 per annum for a certified Luxembourg statutory auditor (if audit threshold exceeded; otherwise not required)

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 0% — SCSp is fiscally transparent; no entity-level corporate income tax. For reference, Luxembourg resident companies are subject to an aggregate CIT rate of 24.94% (Luxembourg City).
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Not subject to CIT; partners are taxed at their applicable marginal rates. Luxembourg offers no statutory tax holiday to SCSp, but transparent treatment avoids investment vehicle withholding; preferential regimes (e.g., IP box 80% exemption) may be available at partner level for qualifying IP.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: ACD Partnership Information Return (SCSp declaration) / MyGuichet.lu eFile (electronic filing portal of Administration des Contributions Directes).
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: By 30 April following the calendar/fiscal year-end; a six-month extension is available on application to the ACD (final deadline 31 October).

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Legal identification of SCSp (registered office, registration number, general partner details).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident SCSp general partner must provide non-resident identification and tax residence country.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Accounting year and fiscal result (allocable partnership profit/loss before tax).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: State Luxembourg-source income and, where DTA applies, the allocation of income to partners.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Partner allocation schedule (name, residence, percentage share, allocated income).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Provide for each non-resident partner: name, address, Luxembourg tax identification if any, and country of residence; attach TRC.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing may trigger an administrative fine up to EUR 1,000 (rising to EUR 2,500 after formal notice); ex officio taxation plus interest at 0.75% per month; persistent non-filing may constitute tax evasion exposing the general partner to criminal penalties.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 15% statutory; 0% for qualifying EU Share-Parent Directive (>=10% participation) or Luxembourg subsidiary exemption; distributions by SCSp are not subject to dividend WHT due to fiscal transparency.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: For partner level treaty relief: submit a claim to the ACD for refund of any withholding tax, attaching the partner's Tax Residence Certificate (TRC), a proof of ownership, and a completed treaty benefit self-declaration. Claims generally must be filed within the Luxembourg statutory limitation period (three years from the end of the calendar year). For SCSp, treaty eligibility is assessed on each underlying partner as beneficial owner.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Luxembourg does not levy domestic withholding tax on outgoing interest or royalty payments to non-residents; treaty rates on interest/royalties are generally 0% / 0% or 10%, subject to DTA and substance.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: EUR 500,000 in annual related-party transactions for Local File; Master File if group consolidated turnover exceeds EUR 750 million.
approved_arm_length_methodologies: CUP, Resale Price, Cost Plus, TNMM, Profit Split
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Luxembourg applies BEPS, EU ATAD and its abuse-of-law doctrine; there is no standalone ESR, but substance over form and beneficial ownership checks are enforced. SCSp must demonstrate real economic activity in Luxembourg (office, employees, decision-making). A pure virtual-office mail scanning SCSp is high-risk.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberately under-reporting or omitting taxable income through the SCSp, or using the fiscally transparent vehicle as a conduit to conceal taxable profit or beneficial ownership from the ACD.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Re-assessment and penalty of 20% to 100% of the tax evaded; criminal fine up to EUR 250,000; imprisonment up to 5 years; seizure/disgorgement of assets.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The SCSp general partner (gérant) is unboundedly and jointly liable for fiscal debts; civil restitution, travel bans, and custodial imprisonment may be imposed on individuals exercising control.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating a 'virtual office' screen using only mail scanning as artificial activity, with no personnel in Luxembourg, to obtain treaty benefits or defer/avoid taxation of underlying investors.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Denial of treaty benefits under the general anti-abuse rule; reclassification of SCSp as taxable company; retroactive interest and penalties up to 100%; deregistration from Luxembourg Commercial Register; ban from certain activities.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors or the general partner may be held personally liable for taxes recalculated under recharacterization; court-imposed management bans and travel restrictions; criminal charges in severe abuse cases.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Providing registered office/mail scanning and management services to foreign companies without obtaining Luxembourg trust or company service provider authorization and failing to apply customer due diligence / beneficial ownership obligations.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under Luxembourg AML Law of 12 November 2004, imprisonment up to 5 years and fines up to EUR 250,000; administrative sanctions from the Minister of Justice/CSSF including license revocation and penalty up to EUR 1,000,000 or 10% of turnover.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Manager/gérant personally exposed to criminal indictment, travel bans, personal fines, confiscation and civil liability for creditors' losses due to breach of AML obligations.
